newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers dip in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers dip in slow trade.

text.p: North American bunker prices dipped from highs last week amid weaker prices abroad on Tuesday and a slight ease in U.S./Iraq tensions, players said.
Trade, however, was quiet, as buyers and sellers held in a standoff amid the unpredictability of whether or not the U.S. will stage another retaliatory attack against Iraq.
The U.S. ordered 3,500 troops to Kuwait on Tuesday.
"Suppliers don't want to come off their numbers and buyers don't want to be left holding expensive barrels. Everyone is waiting for something to happen," said one New York Harbor player.
New York Harbor 380 CST dipped to $117/120 a tonne, down $2 from late last week. The 180 CST grade was quoted at $123/125, a $4 fall.
The Norfolk hub stood about one cent higher compared with New York, with 380 CST at $120/121, and 180 CST at $124/125.
On the Gulf Coast, sentiment was similar amid light demand, with Houston 380 CST at $112/113 a tonne.
Bearishness was more prominent on the West Coast, pressured down not only by the slight ease in U.S./Iraq tension but weaker prices in Singapore.
Los Angeles 380 CST fell $7 to $107/108, traders said.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
